subject: Isolation deployment trade-offs and on-call allocation
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Isolation deployment trade-offs and on-call allocation

Team —

Acme is asking for a dedicated VPC + on-prem runtime option with isolated networking and customer-managed KMS. I collected a first-pass scope in the attached VPC-resourcing-sheet.xlsx and a quick on-call draft (oncall-rotation-draft.pdf). High-level asks from the customer: predictable 99% p99 latency target for interactive endpoints, audit-log retention for 7 years, and a procurement timeline that expects an initial pilot in Q1.

Before I loop in Legal/Compliance formally, I need alignment on two items so we can give ACME a realistic timeline and internal resourcing ask:

- Ownership split: who owns the runtime / incident response vs. customer success vs. security for this offering?
- On-call model: can we support a rotating on-call from Core Serving, or do we require a dedicated SRE for the account for the pilot?

Please review the attachments and call out non-negotiable constraints. Ellen — appreciate any constraints from your side (procurement windows, PoC acceptance criteria).

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: VPC-resourcing-sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, stub), oncall-rotation-draft.pdf (pdf, stub)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Ellen Park <ellen@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Isolation deployment trade-offs and on-call allocation

Marcus —

Quick read-through and my thoughts: we should codify a 3-way ownership model for pilots: Platform (Runtime & deploy automation), Security (baseline hardening, KMS integration, audits), Customer Success (SLO acceptance, runbook handover). For the pilot I recommend we staff:

- Platform: 2 FTE (engineer + tech lead) to own rollout, build deployment automation, and run the initial tuning window.
- SRE on-call: 1 dedicated on-call rota that includes a Core Serving responder; outside normal hours we fall back to a small escalation pool (2 engineers).
- CS: 0.5 FTE (part-time AM) to drive acceptance tests and coordinate audit evidence.

Notes/constraints:
- If we accept a hard 99% p99 SLA for interactive endpoints from day 1 that increases run-costs by ~30% (higher headroom + pre-warming).
- Audit log retention to 7 years requires a separate retention store (we should not cram this into runtime DB). Legal will need to sign off on retention and egress policy.

I created a short Jira ticket to capture the on-call and staffing ask: https://jira.redwood/browse/INFRA-8893 — please add anything missing.

Kimberly
VP, Platform Operations

Date: 2027-12-02T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Isolation deployment trade-offs and on-call allocation

Marcus / Kim —

Adding a few architecture caveats from the runtime side:

- Networking: customer-managed VPC means we can't assume NAT egress patterns; we need an explicit egress and peering plan. That has implications for our caching layer (cross-region caching will be limited).
- KMS/HSM: integration points will likely add 40-80ms crypto overhead on the hot-path unless we proxy key ops; if ACME demands HSM-bound keys we should identify acceptable key-wrapping patterns.
- Quantization & compilation: on-prem GPU types vary — we will need a narrow supported matrix at pilot (e.g., A100, H100 equivalents) and a small compatibility test-suite.

I sketched these in the attached arch-notes-stub.txt. Operationally I think we should treat the pilot as 'Best-effort SLA with formalized escalation' unless Sales accepts a pricing uplift for a guaranteed SLA.

If we go the dedicated SRE route, they must have runbook-level control for restarts, log collection, and escalation hooks; otherwise we will be fighting a lot of ad-hoc handoffs.

Karthik
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime

Attachment: arch-notes-stub.txt (text, stub)

Date: 2027-12-03T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Isolation deployment trade-offs and on-call allocation

Marcus / Team —

Thanks for the clear framing. A few items from Acme's side:

- Procurement timeline: we have budgetary approval to start the SOW in early February; legal needs a compliance appendix and evidence for SOC2 + encryption-in-transit and at-rest.
- SLA expectations: for the pilot we are open to a best-effort SLA with a roadmap to 99% p99 by production rollout, provided we see a detailed remediation plan and a named escalation contact.
- On-call: Acme prefers that Redwood provides a named on-call owner for the pilot (even if it's rotating) and that we have a 30-minute critical-incident response commitment during business hours.

I'll upload the compliance questionnaire to your shared Drive (link to follow) and can start the DocuSign flow once we have the SOW draft.

Ellen
Director of Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Isolation deployment trade-offs and on-call allocation

Thanks — good alignment so far. Quick summary and proposed decision points so we can move the SOW/Procurement process forward:

Decision checkpoint (please ack by EOD Tuesday the 7th):
1) Pilot SLA stance: accept 'best-effort' pilot SLA with documented remediation plan and named escalation owner. (Recommended: YES)
2) Staffing: allocate 2 Platform FTEs for initial rollout, and include Core Serving in a 1-person on-call rotation (escalation pool = 2).
3) Compliance & retention: Security to own the evidence pack; we will provision a separate long-term retention store (not runtime DB).

If we get yes on the three items I'll prepare a short append to the SOW and hand to Legal/Procurement. Also propose a 45-minute alignment call Thursday 12/09 to finalize the on-call rota and confirm the supported GPU matrix.

Ellen — can you confirm DocuSign readiness and whether ACME's procurement can accept a pilot 'best-effort' SLA with a roadmap to guaranteed p99 by prod?

I'll loop in Legal once we have the internal ack.

-Marcus
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
